Bishan

a town of Singapore — sights & hawker food, sourced

Bishan

Bishan 43

  1. Must see · Bishan

    Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery

    Singapore's largest Buddhist monastery, founded 1920 by Venerable Zhuan Dao on Bright Hill (Kong Meng San). Spread over 800,000 sq ft — roughly 14 football fields — its prayer halls, pagodas, Guanyin statue and the ship-like four-storey Venerable Hong Choon Memorial Hall (housing one of Asia's largest bronze Buddha images, 13.8m and 55 tonnes) make it Bishan's great landmark. Also known as Bright Hill Temple.

    Look for Free entry; vegetarian dining hall on site

    88 Bright Hill Road, Singapore 574117

    Recommended by National Library Board, Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Wikipedia

  2. Must see · Hainanese Chicken Rice · Bishan

    Ming Kee Chicken Rice

    The stall most synonymous with Bishan — a 40-plus-year institution beside Bishan Bus Interchange whose chicken is plunged into ice water after poaching for a signature gelatinous skin and tender flesh, drawing snaking queues onto its iconic green plates.

    Kim San Leng Coffee Shop, Blk 511 Bishan Street 13, S570511

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg, HungryGoWhere

  3. Must see · Bishan

    HSBC TreeTop Walk

    The first free-standing suspension bridge of its kind in the region — a 250m span slung 25m high between Bukit Peirce and Bukit Kalang, the two highest points in MacRitchie, for a panoramic view over the rainforest canopy and Upper Peirce Reservoir. A one-way crossing on the wider MacRitchie trail network on Bishan's northern doorstep.

    Look for Free; Tue-Sun ~8.30/9am-5pm, closed Mon

    MacRitchie / Central Catchment Nature Reserve (nearest access via Venus Drive), Singapore

    Recommended by NParks (National Parks Board), National Archives of Singapore

  4. Must see · Bak Kut Teh & Soups · Bishan

    Rong Cheng (Sin Ming Road) Bak Kut Teh

    Uncle Lim has served peppery Teochew bak kut teh here since 1976 and pioneered the use of 'dragon ribs' — the 16 largest rib bones in a pig — in a clear, garlicky, pepper-forward broth that made this remote Sin Ming shop a pilgrimage.

    Blk 22 Sin Ming Road, #01-355, S570022

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Miss Tam Chiak

  5. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Bishan

    Shi Xiang Ge

    Owner Liu Yi Jun was Crystal Jade's La Mian Director for nearly 30 years before opening this humble Shanxi stall atop Bishan Bus Interchange — freshly hand-shaved dao xiao mian and springy la mian in a clear beef-bone broth, plus mala braised-meat noodles.

    Bishan Cafeteria, Bishan Bus Interchange (beside Junction 8), Bishan Place, Singapore

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Miss Tam Chiak, Seth Lui, HungryGoWhere

  6. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Bishan

    Two Chefs Eating Place (Sin Ming)

    The Sin Ming branch of the famed Two Chefs zi char, in a three-storey building in the estate — its signature butter pork ribs are fried crisp and tender then dusted with a slow-cooked butter-milk powder that eats like cereal prawns; other stars include cereal prawn, drunken cockles and coffee pork ribs.

    Blk 409 Sin Ming Avenue, S570409

    Recommended by HungryGoWhere, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), Seth Lui, Daniel Food Diary

  7. Worth the detour · Bishan

    Bishan Public Library

    An architectural landmark by LOOK Architects (opened 2006) conceived as a 'tree house' — 16 brightly coloured pods jut from the facade as suspended reading alcoves, with skylights and coloured glass washing the interior in shifting light. Won Singapore's President's Design Award in 2007 and an International Architecture Award in 2009.

    Look for Free; closed Mondays (check NLB hours)

    5 Bishan Place, #01-01, Singapore 579841

    Recommended by National Library Board, President's Design Award (DesignSingapore), Archello

  8. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Bishan

    Yang Ming Seafood

    The Bishan zi char hotspot that takes over the whole coffeeshop at dinner — its lobster chee cheong fun (silky rice rolls under tender lobster and savoury sauce) won the SPH Food Masters award in 2020; the salt-baked crab is the other must-order.

    Blk 150 Bishan Street 11, S570150

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), Eatbook.sg

  9. Worth the detour · Hainanese Chicken Rice · Bishan

    Leong Hainanese Chicken Rice

    A Shunfu Mart mainstay plating a classic $3.90 Hainanese chicken rice with succulent poached chicken and fragrant, faintly crusty rice — a fixture on every guide to the recently renovated hawker centre.

    Shunfu Mart Food Centre, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui, Her World Singapore

  10. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Bishan

    Lai Heng Fried Kuay Teow

    A long-queuing Shunfu char kway teow stall dishing generous $3 plates of sweet-savoury noodles studded with fresh cockles — one of the food centre's most popular names across post-renovation guides.

    Shunfu Mart Food Centre, #02-20, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary, The Singapore Women's Weekly

  11. Worth the detour · Indian & Roti Prata · Bishan

    Chindamani Indian Restaurant

    A hawker-priced Indian stall that draws steady queues to KPT coffeeshop — its prata dough is kneaded well and cooked thinner and crispier than most, and the $6 chicken biryani comes loaded with a huge, fall-apart curry chicken leg; a shorter-queue alternative to the famous Serangoon North branch.

    KPT Coffeeshop, Blk 284 Bishan Street 22, S570284

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Seth Lui, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost)

  12. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Bishan

    Jiak Mee

    A mee hoon kueh stall run by three 20-year-old friends above Bishan Bus Interchange, hand-tearing dough to order — soupy or dry ban mian, you mian and ee mian with al-dente noodle pieces, minced pork, ikan bilis and a sweet dark sauce; a young-hawker story covered across the food press.

    Bishan Cafeteria, 514 Bishan Street 13, #02-494, S570514

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak

  13. Worth the detour · Kaya Toast, Kopitiam & Breakfast · Bishan

    Sen Yen Charcoal Traditional Toast

    Old-school charcoal-grilled kaya toast in the same Sin Ming kopitiam as Sin Ming Roti Prata — thick, fluffy white loaves toasted over charcoal for a characteristic char, layered with kaya and butter at about $1.20; a Sin Ming breakfast institution.

    Jin Fa (Gim Huat) Kopitiam, 24 Sin Ming Road, #01-51, S570024

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Miss Tam Chiak, Seth Lui

  14. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Bishan

    Hup Seng Duck Rice

    A Sin Ming braised-duck stall with lunchtime queues among the oldest HDB blocks in the estate — tender Teochew-braised duck with a nice layer of fat under a light-but-savoury dark herbal sauce, best paired with the salted-vegetable duck soup, from about $4.50.

    Blk 22 Sin Ming Road, Sin Ming Ville, S570022

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, ladyironchef (Brad Lau), HungryGoWhere

  15. Worth the detour · Bishan

    MacRitchie Reservoir Park

    Singapore's oldest reservoir (1868) fringed by a much-loved park on the edge of the Central Catchment — a boardwalk hugging the water, kayaking, the Chemperai and Prunus trails and a 20km network of nature paths leading to the TreeTop Walk. The green lung directly north of Bishan and Sin Ming.

    Look for Open daily, free

    Lornie Road, Singapore 298717

    Recommended by NParks (National Parks Board), Wikipedia

  16. Worth the detour · Bishan

    Kwong Wai Siew Peck San Theng

    The Cantonese-Hakka cemetery, founded 1870, that gave Bishan its name — 'Peck San Theng' (碧山亭, 'pavilions on the jade hill') became Mandarin 'Bishan'. Once one of Singapore's biggest Chinese cemeteries at 324 acres, it was exhumed from 1982 and rebuilt as a columbarium and preserved ancestral temple; a Heritage Gallery opened in 2018 telling its 150-year story.

    Look for Temple grounds open daily; heritage gallery free

    12 Sin Ming Road, Singapore 575627

    Recommended by Remember Singapore, Wikipedia

  17. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Bishan

    Mei Zhen Hakka Delicacies

    Run by the Toh sisters since the 1980s, this Shunfu stall makes suan pan zi (abacus seeds) with a texture like no other — chewy yam-and-flour discs stir-fried with dried shrimp, minced pork, mushroom and crispy shallots, a hard-to-find Hakka classic.

    Shunfu Mart Food Centre, #02-26, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320

    Recommended by Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), HungryGoWhere

  18. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Bishan

    Sin Kian Heng

    A decades-old Sin Ming heartland stall whose twist is its fishballs — bought fresh daily then fried in the stall's own special oil for a light, springy, browned bite — served over minced-pork noodles with optional braised trotter and intestines.

    Gourmet Street Coffeeshop, Blk 22 Sin Ming Road, S570022

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak

  19. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Bishan

    284 Kway Chap

    One of Bishan's oldest hawker stalls and a cult supper spot — opening in the evening and running into the small hours, its flat rice sheets come with a glossy braise of clean-tasting pig offal that keeps a queue going past midnight.

    Blk 284 Bishan Street 22, Singapore S570284

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, Miss Tam Chiak

  20. Worth the detour · Indonesian, Satay & Rendang · Bishan

    Uncle Penyet (Bishan)

    The Bishan outlet of the well-loved Uncle Penyet chain, tucked into the same Kim San Leng coffeeshop as Ming Kee — a hearty halal plate of crispy-yet-juicy smashed fried chicken over rice with deep-fried tau kwa, greens and a punchy belacan sambal.

    Kim San Leng Coffee Shop, Blk 511 Bishan Street 13, S570511

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui

  21. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Bishan

    Dong Nan Wanton Noodle

    A Shunfu Mart corner stall with no English sign but a constant queue — Malaysian-style dark-sauce wanton mee from $3.50, its springy noodles cooled in cold water before a return to hot, crowned with thick slices of tender char siew; named among Daniel Food Diary's best wanton mee in Singapore.

    Shunfu Mart Food Centre, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary

  22. Deep cut · Bishan

    Bishan ActiveSG Stadium & Sports Centre

    Bishan's public sports hub, run by Sport Singapore's ActiveSG, built around a stadium (opened 1998) with a professional running track that is the main home ground of Singapore Premier League club Lion City Sailors (formerly Home United). The wider centre adds a sports hall, clubhouse courts, swimming pool and a YouthCreates skate spot beside Bishan-AMK Park.

    Look for Public sessions daily; stadium track free when open

    7 Bishan Street 14, Singapore 579784

    Recommended by Wikipedia, AsiaOne, ActiveSG (Sport Singapore)

  23. Deep cut · Bishan

    Old Upper Thomson Road (former Grand Prix circuit)

    The quiet, tree-lined loop on Bishan's northern doorstep that was Singapore's most notorious motor-racing venue — the ~4.9km Thomson Road street circuit hosted the Singapore Grand Prix from 1961 to 1973, with legendary corners named Devil's Bend, The Snakes and Murder Mile. Once lined with kampongs, parts of the old route now thread Thomson Nature Park and skirt Lower Peirce.

    Look for Public road / park connector, open daily, free

    Old Upper Thomson Road, Singapore

    Recommended by National Archives of Singapore, National Library Board, Remember Singapore

  24. Deep cut · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Bishan

    Chocolat N' Spice

    An ex-hotel pastry chef bakes large, moist, fragrant muffins from around $1.50-$2.20 at this Shunfu stall — the Blueberry and Coffee Walnut draw consistent lines, a rare hawker-priced bakery gem.

    Shunfu Mart Food Centre, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui, Her World Singapore

  25. Deep cut · Malay & Nasi Padang · Bishan

    Wak Limah

    Shunfu Mart's comforting no-frills Malay stall running the gamut from nasi lemak to mee rebus, mee soto and lontong — the mee siam, sweet-sour and generously topped, is the pick.

    Shunfu Mart Food Centre, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, The Singapore Women's Weekly, Her World Singapore

  26. Deep cut · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Bishan

    Quan Ann Prawn Mee

    Serving traditional prawn noodles for over 45 years, Quan Ann favours a lighter pork-based broth — the dry version with its robust sauce mix and house-made chilli paste is the crowd favourite at Shunfu.

    Shunfu Mart Food Centre, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Her World Singapore, Seth Lui

  27. Deep cut · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Bishan

    Marsiling Teochew Fish Soup

    A lunchtime-queue stall at Shunfu ladling out refreshing bowls of sliced fish and fried fish soup loaded with vegetables and topped with fried egg — a light, comforting Teochew standard.

    Shunfu Mart Food Centre, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320

    Recommended by The Singapore Women's Weekly, Her World Singapore, Eatbook.sg

  28. Deep cut · Cafés & Modern · Bishan

    Kings Cart Coffee (Bishan Library)

    The Bishan-library outpost of Kings Cart Coffee Factory (of the Joo Chiat roastery) — a peaceful, naturally-lit spot inside the tree-house library for micro-roasted specialty coffee in flavours like matcha, coconut and pandan, plus tea cakes and souffle.

    Bishan Public Library, 5 Bishan Place, Level 1, S579841

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary, The Honeycombers Singapore

  29. Deep cut · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Bishan

    Grin Affair

    A cosy 20-seat dessert cafe beside Bishan MRT from self-taught baker Jody Ang, known for trifle-like cakes layered in reusable glass jars — strawberry-custard, lychee-passionfruit and more — plus meringue waffles whipped from an egg-white-and-soy-milk batter.

    Blk 505D Bishan Street 11, #01-408, S570481

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Time Out Singapore, TheSmartLocal

  30. Deep cut · Bishan

    Central Catchment Nature Reserve

    Singapore's largest nature reserve — some 2,000 hectares of primary and mature secondary rainforest ringing the MacRitchie, Upper/Lower Peirce and Upper Seletar reservoirs. The wild heart of the island on Bishan's northern edge, threaded by the trails, boardwalks and TreeTop Walk that make the town a launchpad for nature outings.

    Look for Trails open daily, free

    Central Singapore (reserve bounded by Upper Thomson, Sin Ming & Island Club roads), Singapore

    Recommended by NParks (National Parks Board), Wikipedia

  31. Deep cut · Bishan

    Junction 8

    Bishan's civic and retail heart, one of Singapore's early suburban malls (soft-opened Nov 1993). Its name nods to Bishan's old MRT station code N8; it debuted with a Daimaru department store, a Golden Village cineplex and Food Junction's very first outlet, and remains the town centre beside Bishan MRT and the bus interchange.

    Look for Open daily ~10am-10pm

    9 Bishan Place, Singapore 579837

    Recommended by Wikipedia, CapitaLand

  32. Deep cut · Bishan

    Tse Tho Aum Temple

    A Buddhist temple at the Sin Ming Drive / Sin Ming Avenue junction that doubles as a crematorium — one of only two privately run cremation facilities in Singapore, the other being at nearby Kong Meng San Phor Kark See. A quiet Sin Ming heritage landmark documented in the National Heritage Board's Roots collection.

    Look for Temple grounds open daily; free

    Junction of Sin Ming Drive & Sin Ming Avenue, Sin Ming, Singapore

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Wikipedia

  33. Deep cut · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Bishan

    Ding Ji Mushroom Minced Meat Noodle

    A Bishan Street 22 coffeeshop stall touted as a worthy alternative to Seng Kee — bak chor mee and a hearty $8 fish maw soup with generous minced pork, pork balls and a higher-grade fish maw in a pork-bone broth.

    Blk 284 Bishan Street 22, Singapore S570284

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Miss Tam Chiak

  34. Deep cut · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Bishan

    Heng Heng Bao Bing

    An unlikely two-in-one Shunfu stall pairing $1.70 handmade popiah with a bowl of fishball noodles — regulars order both — that Daniel Food Diary and Makansutra both flag among the food centre's keepers.

    Shunfu Mart Food Centre, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, Makansutra

  35. Deep cut · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Bishan

    Kam's Roast (Junction 8)

    The Singapore arm of Hong Kong's one-Michelin-star Kam's Roast Goose brings quality Cantonese roast meats to Bishan — roast duck, char siew and crispy roast pork rice from $7.80, with a hefty roast duck drumstick rice at $10.80.

    Food Junction, Junction 8, 9 Bishan Place, #04-01, S579837

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui

  36. Deep cut · Thai · Bishan

    Jai Thai

    A wallet-friendly Bishan-area Thai institution since 1999, serving affordable, honest, family-recipe Thai — zi-char-style plates like phad thai seafood and tom yum seafood well under $10; a long-running student and family staple.

    7 Clover Way, Singapore 579080

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, TheSmartLocal

  37. Deep cut · Thai · Bishan

    Mata Thai Restaurant

    A long-running, wallet-friendly Bishan Thai zi char built for group sharing — its Tom Yum Seafood ($16) arrives bubbling in a claypot overflowing with fresh seafood, and the fried fish comes crisp outside, moist within; most meals land under $10 a head.

    Blk 508 Bishan Street 11, #01-390, S570508

    Recommended by Seth Lui, TheSmartLocal

  38. Deep cut · Thai · Bishan

    Taste of Thailand

    A Thai-inspired zi char in the Midview City industrial canteen where chef Mr Ang's signature is a Thai-style fried kway teow served pad-thai-meets-gravy the way his Sin Ming regulars prefer — alongside a thin, crisp deep-fried fish with chilli dip, all at hidden-gem prices.

    The Canteen @ Midview City, 18 Sin Ming Lane, S573960

    Recommended by Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), Seth Lui

  39. Deep cut · Hawker & Zi Char · Bishan

    Mr Egg Fried Rice

    A hidden Bishan Street 11 stall doing four styles of egg fried rice with five toppings and a wok-hei lift — the savoury, spicy house sambal studded with crispy dried shrimp is what elevates it; portions run generous with a juicy chicken or pork chop.

    New Century Food House, Blk 151 Bishan Street 11, S570151

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak

  40. Deep cut · Cafés & Modern · Bishan

    Thus Coffee

    A hidden indie roastery-cafe on the Sembawang Hills / Upper Thomson edge of Bishan, warmed by wood furnishings — micro-roasted coffee and subtle takes on brunch staples like the Thus Breakfast (sous-vide eggs, hollandaise, apple-cider sausage, back bacon).

    4 Jalan Kuras, S577723

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Time Out Singapore

  41. Deep cut · Hawker & Zi Char · Bishan

    Yue Lai Xiang Delights

    A Sin Ming coffeeshop stall where owner Joy hand-tears colourful mee hoon kueh coloured with real blue pea flowers she grows herself — super-QQ noodles in a robust, MSG-free pork-bone broth with a made-from-scratch chilli dip; a Sin Ming food-trail hidden gem.

    Blk 22 Sin Ming Road, S570022

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost)

  42. Closed — kept for the record · Cafés & Modern · Bishan

    Canopy Garden Dining — CLOSED

    A pet-friendly garden bistro nestled in the greenery of Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park II, its roof planted over with foliage — an all-day casual menu of eggs benedict, buttermilk pancakes and a signature crab aglio olio, a longtime brunch destination in the park.

    1382 Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, Bishan Park II, S569931

    Recommended by HungryGoWhere, The Honeycombers Singapore

  43. Closed — kept for the record · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Bishan

    Denzy Gelato (Bishan) — CLOSED

    A beloved artisanal gelateria across from Bishan Interchange whose Pear, Ginger & Ginger Flower won 'Singapore's Best Gelato' at the Singapore Gelato Championship, its pistachio stone-ground for 10 hours. The Bishan outlet is now permanently closed (the brand continues in Hougang and Bedok); kept here, flagged.

    Blk 506 Bishan Street 13, #01-404, S570506

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui
